requirement: Converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.idempotent` is one sentence: "Converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged." It only describes observable behavior. Converting a record that is already upgraded must leave the file unchanged.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Any implementation that leaves the file unchanged would satisfy it. One could skip upgraded records, rewrite identical bytes, or compare before writing. All of these give the same observable result, so how the code does it is discretionary.

No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so having no implementation roots is not a gap. Tests can cover the behavior.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation: converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.

`src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[loading_is_read_only_and_conversion_is_in_place_idempotent_and_preserves_failures]` is marked `{test}` for it. The test covers the obligation as follows:
- It writes a legacy record and calls `convert_file` once. It asserts that the bytes changed (`assert_ne!(after, before)`), so the record really was upgraded.
- It calls `convert_file` a second time on the upgraded record. It asserts that the file bytes equal the post-first-conversion bytes.
- It also asserts that the file's modification time is unchanged. This catches a second conversion that rewrites the file with identical content.

The tests do not need to cover the input classes of a legacy record or a malformed record here, because the requirement only governs the already-upgraded case. The malformed-file assertions in the test belong to other requirements, such as the one on preserving failures.

I found no obligation that lacks a test or assertion.
